title: The Hidden Risks of the AI Data Center Boom
subtitle: As tech companies build massive new facilities, local communities and safety experts are raising concerns about transparency and emergency preparedness.

summary.en: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving a massive increase in the construction of large data centers. These facilities require significant amounts of electricity and water to operate around the clock. A recent fire at a New York site has highlighted serious safety and accountability issues. While these projects create jobs for many workers, they also face opposition from local communities. Balancing the need for technology with public safety remains a major challenge for the industry.
summary.zh: 人工智慧的快速成長正推動大型資料中心建設的激增。這些設施需要大量的電力與水資源來維持全天候運作。近期紐約一處場址發生的火災，凸顯了嚴重的安全與當責問題。雖然這些計畫為許多勞工創造了就業機會，但也面臨當地社區的強烈反對。如何在技術需求與公共安全之間取得平衡，仍是該產業面臨的一大挑戰。

paragraphs.en: The rapid rise of artificial intelligence is changing the way we live and work, but it is also leading to a massive increase in the number of data centers worldwide. These facilities are large buildings filled with powerful computers that process information for AI tools. Because they must run twenty-four hours a day, they require huge amounts of electricity and water. While this industry creates new jobs, it is also creating new problems for the communities where these centers are built.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智慧的快速崛起正在改變我們的生活與工作方式，但也導致全球資料中心數量大幅增加。這些設施是充滿強大電腦的大型建築，專門為人工智慧工具處理資訊。由於這些電腦必須全天候運作，因此需要消耗大量的電力與水資源。雖然這個產業創造了新的就業機會，但也為這些中心所在的社區帶來了新的問題。

paragraphs.en: In early June, a fire broke out at the Lake Mariner data center in Somerset, New York. This site is a $3.2 billion project built on a former coal mine. The incident exposed serious gaps in how these massive facilities prepare for emergencies. According to Ars Technica, firefighters arrived at the scene to find no working alarm system and no water in the fire hydrants. Even worse, the safety documents that the fire department needed to identify dangerous chemicals had reportedly burned up in the fire.
paragraphs.zh: 六月初，位於紐約州薩默塞特 (Somerset) 的馬里納湖 (Lake Mariner) 資料中心發生火災。該場址是一個耗資三十三億美元、建於廢棄煤礦場上的計畫。這起事件暴露了這些大型設施在應對緊急狀況時存在的嚴重漏洞。根據科技新聞網站 Ars Technica 報導，消防人員抵達現場時，發現警報系統無法運作，消防栓也沒水。更糟的是，據傳消防隊用來辨識危險化學物質的安全文件，也都在火災中燒毀了。

paragraphs.en: Steve Matisz, the chief of the Barker Fire Department, described the experience as very difficult. He explained that his team had to enter the building “kind of blind” because they did not know what chemicals were inside. The lack of information made it hard for them to fight the fire safely. When asked about the situation later in August, Matisz noted that the fire hydrants at the site were still not working correctly. He stated that he had not seen any progress on fixing them, despite promises from the company.
paragraphs.zh: 巴克 (Barker) 消防局局長史蒂夫·馬蒂斯 (Steve Matisz) 形容當時的救援過程非常艱難。他解釋說，由於不清楚建築內存放了哪些化學物質，他的團隊只能「盲目地」進入火場。資訊的匱乏讓他們難以安全地進行滅火工作。當八月稍晚被問及此事時，馬蒂斯指出該場址的消防栓仍無法正常運作。他表示，儘管公司曾做出承諾，但他並未看到任何修復進度。

paragraphs.en: The Lake Mariner project is a complex example of how modern tech companies work together. The site is owned and operated by a company called TeraWulf. Other major players are also involved: Google has agreed to support the project’s future costs, and Anthropic is one of the AI companies that uses the facility to power its technology. TeraWulf told Ars Technica that it is responsible for the safety of the campus. Kerri Langlais, an officer at the company, said they have since added new safety tools, such as special boxes that hold important information for first responders, to improve their emergency plans.
paragraphs.zh: 馬里納湖計畫是一個複雜的案例，顯示了現代科技公司如何相互合作。該場址由一家名為 TeraWulf 的公司擁有並營運。其他主要參與者也牽涉其中：Google 已同意支持該計畫的未來成本，而 Anthropic 則是使用該設施來驅動其技術的人工智慧公司之一。TeraWulf 向 Ars Technica 表示，公司負責該園區的安全。該公司主管凱莉·朗格萊斯 (Kerri Langlais) 表示，他們事後已增設新的安全工具，例如存放重要資訊供第一線應變人員使用的特殊箱子，以改善緊急應變計畫。

paragraphs.en: These safety concerns are occurring at the same time that the industry is facing pressure from local residents. Many communities are trying to block new data center construction because they worry about the impact on their environment and local resources. However, not everyone is against these projects. According to NPR, the boom in data centers has provided a lot of work and extra pay for union electricians. This has created a disagreement between workers who want the jobs and residents who are worried about the safety and environmental effects of these massive buildings.
paragraphs.zh: 這些安全疑慮出現的同時，該產業也正面臨來自當地居民的壓力。許多社區正試圖阻擋新的資料中心建設，因為他們擔心這些設施會對環境與當地資源造成影響。然而，並非所有人都反對這些計畫。根據美國公共廣播電台 (NPR) 報導，資料中心的熱潮為工會電工提供了大量工作機會與額外收入。這導致了想要工作的勞工，與擔心這些大型建築對安全及環境造成影響的居民之間產生了分歧。

paragraphs.en: This situation highlights a larger issue in the tech world: accountability. As AI companies continue to demand more computing power, they are building larger and more complex facilities. When these buildings are constructed quickly, it can be difficult for local officials to keep up with the safety requirements. The fire in New York serves as a warning that the rapid growth of AI infrastructure needs better oversight to protect the people living nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 這種情況凸顯了科技界一個更大的問題：當責性。隨著人工智慧公司持續要求更強大的運算能力，他們正在建造規模更大、結構更複雜的設施。當這些建築被快速興建時，地方官員往往難以跟上安全規範的要求。紐約發生的這場火災是一個警訊，提醒人們人工智慧基礎設施的快速成長需要更好的監督，以保障周邊居民的安全。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the relationship between tech companies and local governments will likely become more tense. As more data centers are planned, communities are asking for more transparency. They want to know exactly what is being built in their neighborhoods and how those companies plan to keep them safe in an emergency. For now, the industry must prove that it can manage its massive energy and water needs without putting public safety at risk. The struggle between the need for technological progress and the safety of local citizens remains a central challenge for the future of artificial intelligence.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，科技公司與地方政府之間的關係可能會變得更加緊張。隨著更多資料中心計畫的推動，社區正要求更高的透明度。他們想確切了解鄰近地區正在興建什麼設施，以及這些公司打算如何確保緊急狀況下的安全。目前，該產業必須證明其能在不危及公共安全的情況下，管理龐大的能源與水資源需求。在追求技術進步與保障當地公民安全之間取得平衡，仍是人工智慧未來發展的核心挑戰。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To start suddenly (usually used for fires, wars, or diseases).
keyTerms.definitionZh: （火災、戰爭、疾病等）突然發生、爆發。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於新聞報導火災，這裡指火災突然發生。文中：In early June, a fire broke out at the Lake Mariner data center in Somerset, New York.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop something from happening or moving forward.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（街區、積木），這裡作動詞用。文中：Many communities are trying to block new data center construction because they worry about the impact on their environment and local resources.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To move or progress at the same speed as something else.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指政府的監管速度趕不上科技發展的速度。文中：When these buildings are constructed quickly, it can be difficult for local officials to keep up with the safety requirements.

previousArticles.summaryEn: The rapid rise of artificial intelligence is leading to a massive increase in the number of data centers worldwide. These facilities require huge amounts of electricity and water to function 24 hours a day. Recent reports show that this demand is putting significant pressure on local power grids and public water supplies. Regulators are now struggling to track this usage due to a lack of transparency from private companies. Experts warn that without better planning, this growth could slow down global efforts to fight climate change.

quiz.question: What specific safety failures did firefighters encounter when responding to the fire at the Lake Mariner data center?

options.A: They were unable to find the building entrance due to thick smoke.
options.B: They lacked access to critical safety documents and functional water supplies.
options.C: The building's automated sprinkler system caused a dangerous electrical surge.
options.D: The company staff refused to provide keys to the chemical storage rooms.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第二段，消防員抵達時發現沒有運作的警報系統、消防栓沒水，且存放化學品資訊的安全文件已在火災中燒毀。選項 A 文章未提及；選項 C 雖然提到火災，但未提及自動灑水系統引發電湧；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章指出是資訊缺乏導致無法辨識化學品，而非人員拒絕給鑰匙。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might local officials struggle to regulate new data centers effectively?

options.A: They lack the legal authority to inspect private technology facilities.
options.B: They are being bribed by major tech companies to ignore safety violations.
options.C: The rapid pace of construction makes it hard for oversight to keep up with development.
options.D: They do not have access to the electricity grid data needed to monitor these sites.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段，文章指出當這些建築物被快速建造時，地方官員很難跟上安全要求，這暗示了建設速度超過了監管能力。選項 A 與文章描述的「需要更好的監督」矛盾；選項 B 文章未提及賄賂；選項 D 雖然提到能源需求，但問題核心在於安全監管而非電力監控。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does the phrase 'kind of blind' mean in the context of the firefighters' experience?

options.A: They were physically unable to see due to the intensity of the fire.
options.B: They were forced to make decisions without essential information.
options.C: They had to rely on their other senses to navigate the building.
options.D: They were not properly trained to handle high-tech facility fires.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文中 Steve Matisz 提到進入建築時是「kind of blind」，隨後解釋是因為不知道裡面有什麼化學品，這顯示「盲目」並非指視力受阻，而是指缺乏關鍵資訊。選項 A 為字面誤解；選項 C 與文章提到的資訊缺失無關；選項 D 雖然消防員可能面臨挑戰，但文中並未批評他們的專業訓練。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the rise of AI data centers?

options.A: The economic benefits of data centers outweigh the environmental concerns for local communities.
options.B: Tech companies like Google and Anthropic are solely responsible for all local safety issues.
options.C: The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure creates a conflict between technological growth and public safety.
options.D: Local governments should completely stop the construction of new data centers to ensure safety.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章從頭至尾都在討論 AI 資料中心帶來的經濟利益（工作機會）與其引發的環境及安全隱憂（火災、資源消耗），並在最後一段總結這是一個「技術進步與公民安全之間」的鬥爭。選項 A 過於偏頗；選項 B 忽略了營運商 TeraWulf 的責任；選項 D 過於極端，文章強調的是需要更好的監督與透明度，而非全面停止建設。
